plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plain vector diagram of four arrows stacked one above another, all drawn at the same shallow upward slope so their lengths can be compared at a glance. Each arrow starts from a small filled black dot. The topmost arrow, in dark navy, is by far the longest and is labeled 3v at its head. Below it an orange arrow labeled v runs in the same up-and-to-the-right direction at about a third that length. Beneath the orange one, a teal arrow labeled 1/2 v is half as long as v and again points the same way. The bottom arrow, drawn in red and labeled -v, has its dot at the right end and its arrowhead at the left, so it runs down and to the left while staying parallel to the others and matching v in length. Because all four share a single line of action, the only difference the eye registers is length, plus the reversal in the last one. The arrangement gives the geometric reading of multiplying a vector by a scalar: a positive factor stretches or shrinks the arrow while preserving its heading, and a negative factor turns it back on itself.

interactionPlan.concept: Multiplying a vector by a scalar stretches or shrinks its length while preserving its direction when the scalar is positive, and reverses its direction when the scalar is negative.
elements: navy arrow 3v — longest, starting from a filled black dot, labeled '3v' at its head
orange arrow v — one third the length of 3v, same slope, labeled 'v' at its head
teal arrow ½v — half the length of v, same slope, labeled '½v' at its head
red arrow −v — same length as v but pointing down-and-to-the-left, dot at the right end, labeled '−v' at its head
filled black dot at the tail of each arrow (four dots, one per row)
dynamic purple arrow kv driven by the scalar slider, with its own dot and a head label that updates with k
shared common-tail origin marker used in overlay view

interactions.label: Scalar multiplier k
interactions.teaches: The learner sees that positive k stretches or shrinks the arrow along the same heading, k = 0 collapses the vector to a point, and negative k flips the arrow to point the opposite way

interactions.label: Layout
interactions.teaches: Placing all arrows on a common tail lines their tips up along one ray, making it obvious that every positive multiple of v points the same way and only negative multiples reverse direction

demo_steps.title: Same direction, different lengths
demo_steps.narration: All four arrows lie on the same shallow slope. 3v, v, and ½v all point up-and-to-the-right — only their lengths differ, in exact proportion to the scalar.

demo_steps.title: Scale the vector with k
demo_steps.narration: Drag k upward and the arrow stretches toward 3v; drag it toward 0 and it shrinks to the origin dot. The heading never changes while k stays positive.

demo_steps.title: Cross zero and reverse
demo_steps.narration: Push k below 0: the arrow flips to point down-and-to-the-left, exactly like the red −v arrow. A negative scalar reverses direction; |k| still sets the length.

demo_steps.title: Overlay on one tail
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the shared-tail view: every arrow now starts at the same dot, so their tips line up along a single ray for positive k and along the opposite ray for negative k.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A positive scalar only changes a vector's magnitude, a negative scalar flips its direction 180°, and k = 0 annihilates it — a scalar never rotates a vector to a new heading.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the four static arrows stacked vertically with generous spacing, all on the same shallow up-and-to-the-right slope (~10–15° above horizontal). Colors and labels exactly as in the figure: navy 3v (longest), orange v, teal ½v, red −v (reversed, dot at right end, arrowhead at left, labeled '−v'). Small filled black dots mark each tail. Add a fifth slider-driven arrow in a distinct highlighted color (purple), labeled 'kv' with the label updating live (e.g. '2.25v', '−0.75v'). In Shared-tail mode, move all tails to one emphasized origin dot with a faint dashed extension line through it showing both rays. Animate length and flip transitions smoothly as the slider moves; at k = 0 the arrow collapses to the dot itself with a small '0' label.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for scalar multiplier k: the learner drags k from negative to positive values, the arrow length scales and flips direction when k crosses 0, and scalar multiplication is seen as stretching, shrinking, or reversing a vector.
